US Requires Licenses for AI Chip Exports to China

2026-W46 6 outlets SRQ
0.64 V2×13

The Trump administration introduced an interim rule requiring export licenses for advanced AI chips and remote computing access that could benefit China or other restricted nations.

Full Narration

Any firm that wants to export advanced AI chips to China, or route computing access through China via a third country, now needs a U.S. government license to do it. The Trump administration implemented an interim rule this week closing that loophole, according to PBS NewsHour. The rule also extends export license requirements to Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore, and Brazil — countries that could otherwise serve as pass-through points for restricted computing access. Here's what matters: the target isn't just direct chip shipments. It's remote access to U.S. servers that run AI workloads. A company in Shanghai logging into a data center in Singapore would now fall under this rule. The license requirement is in effect now, under the interim designation.

DOMESTIC_POLITICS

Scott Colom Wins Mississippi Senate Race for Democrats

2026-W46 13 outlets SRQ
0.91 V1×13 V2×3 V3×3 V4×1

Scott Colom defeated Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith to become Mississippi's first Black U.S. senator since the Reconstruction era.

Full Narration

Democrat Scott Colom won Mississippi's U.S. Senate race this week, defeating Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith. Colom is the first Black U.S. senator from Mississippi since the Reconstruction era, verified by multiple fact-checkers. Mississippi has not sent a Black senator to Washington since the post-Civil War Reconstruction period — a gap of more than 140 years. Colom's win flips a Senate seat in a state that has voted Republican in presidential elections for decades. The question now is what this result signals for Democratic competitiveness in deep-South states ahead of the next election cycle. Colom will fill a full Senate term.
